outputs.body:
Parent tracking issue: #3601 Parent Temporal epic: #39  ## Goal  Adopt Temporal Worker Versioning build-ID routing and pin in-flight executions to compatible implementations.  ## Scope  - Map the existing Goobers worker/build identity (#632, closed) onto Temporal build IDs and versioned task-queue routing. - Pin in-flight executions to a compatible workflow/activity implementation across deploys and resumes. - Surface the worker/build that executed each workflow/activity attempt in the journal, telemetry, and Temporal metadata.  ## Acceptance criteria  - In-flight executions remain deterministic and routable during a rolling upgrade. - An operator can explain which build executed every workflow/activity attempt. - Tests cover mixed worker fleets, long-running workflows, and resume.  ## Notes  Prerequisites #632 and #2911 are closed. Rollout lifecycle (ramp/drain/rollback) and IR-version admission are tracked as sibling children of #3601. Journal/telemetry additions here are additive.    ## Current remediation scope (2026-09-08)  The prior implementation passed review, including mixed-fleet and resume coverage, but was discarded after an environment-only missing-sh CI failure. Recreate the full accepted implementation; Git sh is now on native CI PATH.     ## Escalation correction (2026-09-08)  Recreate the full implementation and address these exact remaining gaps before completion:  - Record build and executing-worker identity for every workflow attempt and every activity attempt, including failed activity attempts; a successful ResultEnvelope-only decorator is insufficient. - Expose the attempt identity consistently in the journal and applicable telemetry/Temporal metadata. - Add behavioral regression tests for mixed worker fleets during rolling upgrade, deterministic long-running workflow pinning, resume, and failed-attempt visibility. Static worker-option assertions are insufficient.     ## Behavioral-routing correction (2026-09-08)  Recreate the accepted build/worker journal and telemetry wiring, then add a behavioral Temporal versioning test that cannot pass when routing is broken. The test must run old/new versioned workers as a mixed fleet, start a long-running workflow on the old build, introduce the new build, and verify subsequent/resumed activity attempts remain deterministically pinned as required, including failed-attempt identity visibility. Passing BuildID as workflow input or directly invoking interceptors is not sufficient.     ## Ready-worker proof correction (2026-09-08)  The production identity and error-metadata wiring is accepted. Complete only the remaining behavioral-test gap: before signaling the pinned old-build workflow during the new-worker-only window, positively prove the incompatible new worker is actively polling and can execute an unpinned probe workflow/activity on that same queue. Then demonstrate the pinned workflow's resumed work remains unroutable to the new build until an old-build worker returns. A fixed startup timeout or an unverified schedule-to-start timeout is insufficient.   ## Deterministic readiness-barrier correction (2026-09-09)  Recreate the latest real mixed-fleet Temporal test and replace timing assumptions with deterministic readiness barriers:  - Do not rely on a fixed timeout immediately after compatibility registration to prove the old-build worker is ready. - After restoring the old-build worker, positively prove versioning propagation and worker availability before awaiting the pinned workflow's resumed result; never use an unbounded final `run.Get`. - The test must reliably prove the new build can execute an unpinned probe while pinned old-build work remains unroutable, then completes once a proven-ready old-build worker returns. - Preserve the accepted production build/worker attempt identity, cancellation handling, and stage-span branch attribution. ## Interrupted-review correction (2026-09-09)  Preserve and recreate the latest implementation from run `ddbef7b41fb3a14946ea1239b81cce47`; its fourth implementation produced a non-empty reviewer diff (`sha256:a6b23eb61fdb0902492b7b4117f9298c697c10b501bb2ac3d3c1707c9087b30c`, 20,305 bytes), but the daemon restart interrupted review attempt 4. Recovery exhausted the repass budget using the prior needs-changes verdict without evaluating that latest diff. The next run must restore the latest work and obtain a real review against the deterministic mixed-fleet/readiness-barrier requirements; do not treat the interrupted review as a substantive rejection or return no-work. ## Serialized Windows CI retry correction (2026-09-10)  Preserve the review-passed implementation from run `26f711e272ada35938fd67537df5a4be`, accepted diff `sha256:fd909068ae32a37ffb531410372ab8c4764ed042946336f76d38191d3a38de58` (79,299 bytes). The final review passed the deterministic mixed-fleet Temporal readiness proof and additive attempt-identity propagation.  The terminal local-CI failure was environmental: formatting, vet, complexity (`188/188`), shipped-workflow contracts, and earlier checks passed, then the repository-wide test fanout failed when `runtime/cgo` reported `cgo.exe: exit status 2`, causing unrelated packages to report build failures. Evidence is stdout digest `sha256:d187ae3b7d1fc60fc7dceb132ae01b9aba7c4b066614fcf370dc242a96abd5ba`; stderr is empty. Restore the unchanged accepted patch and rerun under the corrected `project-ci` Windows wrapper, which serializes native CI and prevents competing local-CI processes. Do not rewrite the accepted behavior or return no-work while the reviewed diff still needs publication.  ## Literal dependency-guard correction (2026-09-16)  Preserve the mandatory-review-passed production implementation and behavioral mixed-fleet test. The remaining deterministic local-CI failure is source-level dependency policy, not behavior: in `internal/workerhost/versioning_integration_test.go`, replace `testdep.RequireEnv(t, temporaltest.CLIEnvVar)` with the literal call `testdep.RequireEnv(t, "GOOBERS_TEMPORAL_CLI")`. The guard requires a string literal at the call site. Obtain fresh mandatory review and full CI after this one-line correction; do not restore an older unchanged commit. 
## Portal-test retry correction (2026-09-16)

Preserve mandatory-review-passed commit `2d6144376c5b15d810543853b1ce98b9d0cab95a` and diff `sha256:f0549ecba83207b360144621e4c3c1601dbf46ce7e3e3b782eb3d23defcf6421`; it includes the required literal `testdep.RequireEnv(t, "GOOBERS_TEMPORAL_CLI")`. Full local CI advanced past the dependency guard and failed only one unrelated portal test: `src/pages/RunsPagePagination.test.tsx` (`drops a targeted refresh that no longer matches the selected filter`, line 317), while 654 other portal tests passed. Restore the unchanged reviewed commit and rerun full serialized CI; do not rewrite the accepted #4083 implementation.
